item.title: One Year After Busan: Has China Kept Its Rare Earth Promises?
item.description: One year after Busan, China’s rare earth exports to the United States remain sharply below pre-restriction levels, even as global shipments hold steady. Beijing’s continued control over rare earth supplies raises the stakes for Trump-Xi meetings in Shenzhen and Miami.

item.title: Mind the Gap: Keeping Export Compliance Within Reach as BIS Focuses on Enforcement
item.description: The Department of Commerce is emphasizing enforcement of export controls and engaging less with industry. CSIS and UGA experts lay out four steps to keep the resulting compliance burden manageable.

item.title: Contested Skies: What a Recent Military Operation with Mexico Reveals About the Homeland Drone Fight
item.description: A novel operation along the southwest border to counter cartel drones demonstrated homeland drone defense that centers the U.S. military in a law enforcement role. This analysis examines Operation High Eagle and its implications for U.S. ability to defend against drones.

item.title: Trilateral “Denuclearization”: False Promises or Way Forward?
item.description: The Trump administration wants denuclearization on the agenda for potential talks with Putin and Xi at APEC. Washington should use the talks to lay the groundwork for trilateral arms control, promote transparency, and out-compete Beijing and Moscow in nuclear diplomacy.

item.title: CSIS Press Briefing: Previewing President Trump's Trip to Asia
item.description: The Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) hosted a virtual press briefing to preview President Trump's upcoming Asia trip (November 16-19).

item.title: National Security Cannot Be an Afterthought in Antitrust Enforcement
item.description: Antitrust remedies can reshape U.S. tech leadership relative to China. National security experts should assess those consequences before the government commits to enforcement, not after.

item.title: Lebanon’s Imperiled Transition: The Need for an Urgent Reset
item.description: As Lebanon approaches the two-year mark of the new leadership’s mandate, progress toward real sovereignty and fundamental reform appears dangerously stalled. An urgent strategic reboot is necessary.
